headline: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (2026, 26.5GB Q5_K_M) on a 16GB MacBook Air: stock llama.cpp/Ollama engine cannot run it at all; our engine runs it at 8.3 tok/s using a 2.9GB expert cache
model: unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF UD-Q5_K_M (26.46GB; 40 layers x 256 experts, k=8, shared expert, hybrid linear-attention trunk; arch qwen3_5_moe)
machine: MacBook Air M2 16GB, internal SSD, CPU backend, n_ubatch=1

stock_baseline.driver_mmap_ubatch512: SIGKILL (exit 137) - macOS killed it during model load
stock_baseline.verdict: DNF - the model does not fit and the OS-paged fallback is unusable

slots32_margin_002.note: compute-bound: matches slots64 - margin router pushed I/O below the CPU compute floor

slots88_margin_002.note: slightly slower than slots32: memory pressure on 16GB machine outweighs extra hits

interpretation: total RAM in the winning config ~6GB (2.9 expert cache + ~3 trunk mmap + KV) for a 26.5GB model
estimated CPU compute ceiling for ~3B active params at Q5 on M2 is ~9-11 tok/s; 8.3 achieved = ~80% of the physical ceiling of the machine itself

quality: m=0 mode is exact routing (bit-exactness proven on OLMoE where a resident reference fits; impossible to run a resident reference for this model on this machine - that is the point); m=0.02 output verified coherent and correct

the garbage-output bug during bring-up was a missing llmstream_alloc() in the qwen35moe adapter - slot tensors landed in scheduler scratch memory; driver now fails loudly if an adapter forgets allocation
